chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and from Yunus from Ibn Mukhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The Fitrah (alms of breaking the fast) upon every people is from what they feed their dependents, from milk or raisins or other than them.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةُ: Zakat al-Fitr, the alms-tax paid at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What determines the staple food of a community for Zakat al-Fitr
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the principle of *al-'urf* (custom) in Shia jurisprudence, linking the obligation of Zakat al-Fitr to the local staple diet rather than a fixed universal commodity. By citing milk, raisins, or other sustenance, it highlights the juristic flexibility to accommodate regional economic and agricultural variations, ensuring the charity remains accessible and meaningful to the specific community.
